records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּהַ֥ר סִינַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses on [the] mountain of Sinai, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses on Mount Sinai,

decisions.choice: on Mount Sinai: these laws are given at the mountain
decisions.reason: Most of Leviticus is spoken from the tent of meeting (1:1). This speech, like the summary in 7:38 and the closing words in 26:46 and 27:34, is set at Mount Sinai itself, where the covenant was made (Exodus 19-24). The laws of the sabbath year and the Jubilee are tied to that covenant, and the blessings and curses of chapter 26 follow them.

records.heading: The Sabbath year

records.source: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י תָבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם וְשָׁבְתָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and you will say to them, when you come into the land which I [am] giving to you, and will rest the land a sabbath to Yahweh.
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When you enter the land I am giving you, the land is to have a Sabbath rest in honor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you come into the land which I am giving you, the land shall rest a sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'When you enter the land I am giving you, the land must rest. Its Sabbath rest will honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the land shall rest a sabbath: the land itself keeps a time of rest
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "sabbath" comes; it means to stop or rest. As people rest on the seventh day (23:3; Exodus 20:8-11), the land is to rest in the seventh year. The rest is "to the LORD": it is kept for him and belongs to him, as the weekly Sabbath does. Exodus 23:10-11 gives the first form of this law.

decisions.choice: which I am giving you: the land is God's gift
decisions.reason: The land is spoken of as God's gift from the first verse of the law. Verse 23 draws the conclusion: the land belongs to God, and Israel holds it from him.

decisions.choice: in honor of / will honor the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "to the LORD" means kept for him and dedicated to him. Balanced and Readable say "in honor of" so that it is not read as rest given to the LORD.

records.source: שֵׁ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ תִּזְרַ֣ע שָׂדֶ֔ךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְמֹ֣ר כַּרְמֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Six years you will sow your field, and six years you will prune your vineyard and you will gather its produce.
pieces: For six years you may plant your fields and trim your vineyards and gather what they yield.

L.3: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its produce.

R.3: For six years you may plant your fields, trim your grapevines, and gather your crops.

decisions.choice: prune: cut back the vine
decisions.reason: The verb means to trim or cut back vines so they bear well (Isaiah 5:6). With sowing, it stands for all the ordinary work of farming fields and vineyards.

decisions.choice: you may plant
decisions.reason: The Hebrew future here grants permission rather than giving an order; the command is in verse 4. Balanced and Readable say "you may".

records.source: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ת שַׁבַּ֤ת שַׁבָּתוֹן֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֑ה שָֽׂדְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔ע וְכַרְמְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תִזְמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And in the year the seventh a sabbath of sabbath rest will be for the land, a sabbath to Yahweh; your field not you will sow, and your vineyard not you will prune.
pieces: But the seventh year is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when you neither sow your fields nor prune your vineyards.

L.4: But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath of sabbath rest for the land, a sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; your field you shall not sow, and your vineyard you shall not prune.

R.4: But the seventh year must be a year of complete rest for the land. It is a Sabbath for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Do not plant your fields or trim your grapevines that year.

decisions.choice: a sabbath of sabbath rest: a complete rest
decisions.reason: Joining the noun to a fuller form of the same word makes it stronger: a full and solemn rest. The same phrase is used of the weekly Sabbath (23:3) and the Day of Atonement (16:31; 23:32). Here it is applied to a whole year.

decisions.choice: a year of complete rest
decisions.reason: Readable says "a year" where the settled wording for days is "a day of complete rest", since it is the seventh year that rests.

records.source: אֵ֣ת סְפִ֤יחַ קְצִֽירְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִקְצ֔וֹר וְאֶת־עִנְּבֵ֥י נְזִירֶ֖ךָ לֹ֣א תִבְצֹ֑ר שְׁנַ֥ת שַׁבָּת֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֥ה לָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: The self-sown grain of your harvest not you will harvest, and the grapes of your untrimmed vine not you will gather; a year of sabbath rest will be for the land.
pieces: Do not harvest the grain that comes up on its own from the last crop, and do not pick the grapes from the vines you have left unpruned. It is to be a year of complete rest for the land.

L.5: The aftergrowth of your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your untrimmed vine you shall not gather; a year of sabbath rest it shall be for the land.

R.5: Do not cut the grain that grows by itself from seeds that fell the year before. Do not pick the grapes from the vines you did not trim. The land must have a year of complete rest.

decisions.choice: aftergrowth: grain that springs up by itself
decisions.reason: The word means grain that grows on its own from seed dropped at the last harvest, without being sown (2 Kings 19:29; Isaiah 37:30).

decisions.choice: your untrimmed vine: a vine left uncut, like a Nazirite's hair
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a Nazirite, a person set apart by a vow whose hair is left uncut (Numbers 6:5). A vine left unpruned in the seventh year is pictured in the same way: set apart and left untouched. Verse 11 uses it again for the Jubilee.

decisions.choice: not reap, not gather: no harvesting as owners do
decisions.reason: Verse 6 says that what the land produces in this year will be food for everyone. So what is forbidden is the regular harvest by the owner for storage and sale; people may still eat what grows (compare Exodus 23:11).

records.source: וְ֠הָיְתָה שַׁבַּ֨ת הָאָ֤רֶץ לָכֶם֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה לְךָ֖ וּלְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וְלַאֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלִשְׂכִֽירְךָ֙ וּלְתוֹשָׁ֣בְךָ֔ הַגָּרִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And will be the sabbath of the land for you for food, for you and for your slave and for your female slave and for your hired laborer and for your settler, the [ones] sojourning with you,
pieces: Whatever the land produces in its Sabbath year will be food for all of you: for you, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the resident who stays with you,

L.6: And the sabbath [produce] of the land shall be food for you, for you and for your male slave and for your female slave and for your hired worker and for your settler who sojourns with you,

R.6: During that Sabbath year, whatever grows on the land will be food for everyone. It will feed you, your male and female servants, your hired workers, and the people who live among you.

decisions.choice: the sabbath of the land: what the land produces in its sabbath year
decisions.reason: The phrase means what grows by itself in the year of rest. It is not stored by the owner but shared by all who live on the land, people and animals alike (verse 7; Exodus 23:11).

decisions.choice: slave, hired worker, settler: everyone who lives and works on the land
decisions.reason: The list names the dependents of an Israelite household: slaves who belonged to it (see verse 44 on their position), workers paid by the day or the year (19:13), and the settler, a free person without land of his own (see verse 23). All of them eat from the seventh-year growth on equal terms with the owner.

decisions.choice: the resident who stays with you / the people who live among you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "your settler who sojourns with you". Balanced uses the settled "resident" and Readable "people who live among you" (see verse 23); the verb "sojourn" is covered by "stays with you" and "live among you".

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The meaning decision (m2) keeps that they belonged to the household, unlike the hired worker.

records.source: וְלִ֨בְהֶמְתְּךָ֔ וְלַֽחַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ תִּהְיֶ֥ה כָל־תְּבוּאָתָ֖הּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃ס
records.gloss: and for your livestock and for the animal[s] which [are] in your land will be all its produce to eat.
pieces: and for your livestock and for the wild animals in your land. All that the land yields may be eaten.

L.7: and for your livestock and for the wild animals which [are] in your land all its produce shall be for eating.

R.7: It will also feed your farm animals and the wild animals in your land. Anything the land produces may be eaten.

decisions.choice: animals: wild animals
decisions.reason: The word means living creatures and, set beside livestock, the wild animals of the countryside. Exodus 23:11 says the same: what the poor leave, the wild animals may eat.

records.source: וְסָפַרְתָּ֣ לְךָ֗ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת שָׁנִ֔ים שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְהָי֣וּ לְךָ֗ יְמֵי֙ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תֵּ֥שַׁע וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, and will be to you the days of seven sabbaths of the years nine and forty years.
pieces: Count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years. The time of the seven Sabbaths of years will come to forty-nine years.

L.8: And you shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, and the days of the seven sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.

R.8: Count seven groups of seven years. That makes forty-nine years in all.

decisions.choice: sabbaths of years: weeks of years, each ending in a sabbath year
decisions.reason: "Sabbath" can mean a week, the seven days that end with the Sabbath (23:15). Here it is a set of seven years ending with the seventh, the sabbath year of verses 2-7. Seven such sets make forty-nine years.

decisions.choice: seven groups of seven years
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means, since "Sabbaths of years" would puzzle a young reader.

records.heading: The year of Jubilee

records.source: וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֞ שׁוֹפַ֤ר תְּרוּעָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֖וֹר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בְּיוֹם֙ הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים תַּעֲבִ֥ירוּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּכָל־אַרְצְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will cause to pass a ram's horn of loud blast in the month the seventh, on the tenth of the month; on [the] day of the atonements you will cause to pass a ram's horn in all your land.
pieces: Then on the tenth day of the seventh month send the loud blast of the ram's horn out across the country. On the Day of Atonement have the horn sounded through all your land.

L.9: Then you shall sound a ram's horn of loud blast in the seventh month, on the tenth [day] of the month; on the day of atonement you shall sound a ram's horn through all your land.

R.9: Then on the tenth day of the seventh month, blow a ram's horn loudly. Do it on the Day of Atonement. Let the sound of the horn go through all your land.

decisions.choice: cause a ram's horn of loud blast to pass: send its sound everywhere
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something pass through. The sound of the horn is passed on from place to place until it has gone through all the land, so that everyone knows the Jubilee has begun. The horn's "loud blast" is the sound that announces an event (23:24; Numbers 10:5-6).

decisions.choice: the Day of Atonement: the Jubilee begins on the day of cleansing
decisions.reason: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement (16:29-31; 23:27). The year of release begins on the day when the sanctuary and the people are cleansed of their sins. The plural "atonements" is the usual form of the name (23:27-28).

decisions.choice: the seventh month: in the autumn
decisions.reason: Counting from the spring (Exodus 12:2), the seventh month falls in September or October, after the harvest and before the new sowing. The farming year began in the autumn, so the year of rest begins there too.

decisions.choice: across the country / through all your land
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "cause to pass" in both halves of the verse: the sound is to travel through the land.

records.source: וְקִדַּשְׁתֶּ֗ם אֵ֣ת שְׁנַ֤ת הַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּקְרָאתֶ֥ם דְּר֛וֹר בָּאָ֖רֶץ לְכָל־יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ יוֹבֵ֥ל הִוא֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְשַׁבְתֶּ֗ם אִ֚ישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּת֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ תָּשֻֽׁבוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will consecrate the year of the fifty year[s], and you will proclaim release in the land to all its inhabitants; a jubilee it will be for you, and you will return each man to his possession, and each man to his clan you will return.
pieces: Set the fiftieth year apart as holy, and announce freedom in the land for everyone who lives in it. This will be your Jubilee, when each of you goes home to your own property and to your own clan.

L.10: And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants; it shall be a Jubilee for you, and you shall return, {{gender:each one|each man}} to his possession, and {{gender:each one|each man}} to his clan you shall return.

R.10: Set apart the fiftieth year as holy. Announce freedom in the land for all the people who live there. It will be your Year of Jubilee. Each of you will go back to your family's land and to your own clan.

decisions.choice: Jubilee: the year named after the ram's horn
alternatives: the year of the ram's horn
decisions.reason: The word means a ram, or a ram's horn: in Joshua 6:4-6 the priests blow "horns of rams" using this word, and in Exodus 19:13 it is the horn that sounds at Sinai. The fiftieth year takes its name from the horn that announces it (verse 9). In this year land that has been sold goes back to the family that held it (verses 13, 28), and Israelites who have sold themselves go free (verses 40-41, 54)..

decisions.choice: liberty: release, setting free
decisions.reason: The word means release, and especially the freeing of people held for debt. It is used again of freeing slaves in Jeremiah 34:8, 15, 17, of "the year of release" in Ezekiel 46:17, and of good news for captives in Isaiah 61:1, the passage Jesus reads in Luke 4:18-19. It is related to the word used in ancient Mesopotamian royal decrees that cancelled debts. Here the release is for people and for land alike: every family is restored to its land and its freedom.

decisions.choice: the fiftieth year: the year after the seventh sabbath year
decisions.reason: The Jubilee is the fiftieth year, the year after the forty-ninth (verse 8). As the fiftieth day follows seven weeks in 23:15-16, this year follows seven sets of seven years. Since the forty-ninth year is itself a sabbath year, the land rests two years in a row, as verses 21-22 provide for in the case of a single sabbath year. Whether the fiftieth year was counted as the first year of the next cycle the text does not say.

decisions.choice: possession, clan: the family's land and the wider family group
decisions.reason: The "possession" is the land a family held as its share of Israel's land (Numbers 26:52-56; Joshua 13-19). The "clan" is the group of related households within a tribe. In the Jubilee each household is restored to both: its land and its place among its kin.

decisions.choice: announce freedom
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "freedom", the plain sense of the word; Literal keeps the traditional "liberty".

records.source: יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֗וא שְׁנַ֛ת הַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔עוּ וְלֹ֤א תִקְצְרוּ֙ אֶת־סְפִיחֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א תִבְצְר֖וּ אֶת־נְזִרֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: A jubilee it, the year of the fifty year[s], will be for you; not you will sow, and not you will harvest its self-sown grain, and not you will gather its untrimmed vines.
pieces: That fiftieth year is to be your Jubilee. Do not sow, and do not harvest what springs up by itself or pick the grapes from the unpruned vines.

L.11: A Jubilee it, the fiftieth year, shall be for you; you shall not sow, and you shall not reap its aftergrowth, and you shall not gather [the grapes of] its untrimmed vines.

R.11: The fiftieth year will be your Jubilee. Do not plant anything. Do not cut the grain that grows by itself, or pick the grapes from the vines nobody trimmed.

decisions.choice: not sow, not reap, not gather: the rules of the seventh year apply
decisions.reason: The words repeat verses 4-5: the Jubilee is kept like a sabbath year, and the land rests (see verse 10 on the two years of rest).

records.source: כִּ֚י יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֔וא קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־הַ֨שָּׂדֶ֔ה תֹּאכְל֖וּ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For a jubilee it [is]; holy it will be to you; from the field you will eat its produce.
pieces: For it is a Jubilee, and it is to be holy to you. Eat what the field gives, straight from the field.

L.12: For it [is] a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you; from the field you shall eat its produce.

R.12: It is a Jubilee, a holy year for you. Eat only what grows in the fields by itself.

decisions.choice: from the field you shall eat: eat what grows, not what is stored
decisions.reason: The produce is eaten where it grows, taken day by day as needed, not harvested and stored by the owner (compare verses 5-7).

decisions.choice: only what grows ... by itself
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the point of "from the field" from verses 5 and 11: the food is what grows on its own and is picked as needed.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הַיּוֹבֵ֖ל הַזֹּ֑את תָּשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: In [the] year of the jubilee the this you will return each man to his possession.
pieces: This Jubilee year is when each of you goes home to your own property.

L.13: In this year of the Jubilee you shall return, {{gender:each one|each man}} to his possession.

R.13: In this Year of Jubilee, each of you will go back to your own land.

decisions.choice: return to his possession: land sold goes back to the family
decisions.reason: This verse states the heart of the Jubilee, set out in verses 14-34: no family's land can be lost for good. Whatever has been sold returns to the household that held it.

records.source: וְכִֽי־תִמְכְּר֤וּ מִמְכָּר֙ לַעֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ א֥וֹ קָנֹ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ אַל־תּוֹנ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And when you sell a thing sold to your fellow citizen or buy from [the] hand of your fellow citizen, not you will wrong each man his brother.
pieces: When you sell land to your neighbor or buy it from your neighbor, do not cheat one another.

L.14: And when you sell something to your fellow or buy from the hand of your fellow, you shall not wrong, {{gender:each one|each man}}, his brother.

R.14: When you sell land to your neighbor or buy land from your neighbor, do not cheat each other.

decisions.choice: wrong: oppress, take unfair advantage
decisions.reason: The verb means to mistreat or oppress, often by using power or need against someone. It is used of mistreating the outsider (Exodus 22:21; Leviticus 19:33). Here it means using the sale to cheat the other person, as verses 15-16 explain.

decisions.choice: your fellow, his brother: another Israelite
decisions.reason: The word for "fellow" means a member of the same community (19:11, 15). "Brother" here means a fellow Israelite, as through the rest of the chapter.

decisions.choice: land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "a thing sold". Verses 15-16 show that the sale of land is meant, so Balanced and Readable say "land".

records.source: בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שָׁנִים֙ אַחַ֣ר הַיּוֹבֵ֔ל תִּקְנֶ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר שְׁנֵֽי־תְבוּאֹ֖ת יִמְכָּר־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: By [the] number of years after the jubilee you will buy from your fellow citizen; by [the] number of years of produce he will sell to you.
pieces: The price you pay your neighbor is to depend on how many years have gone by since the Jubilee, and the price he asks is to depend on how many years of harvests remain.

L.15: By the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your fellow; by the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.

R.15: When you buy land, count the years since the last Jubilee. The seller must set the price by the number of harvests left before the next Jubilee.

decisions.choice: by the number of years of crops: the price is for the harvests until the Jubilee
decisions.reason: Because the land returns to its family at the Jubilee, a buyer is really paying for the use of the land until then. The price is worked out by the number of harvests he will gather from it.

decisions.choice: before the next Jubilee
decisions.reason: Readable adds "before the next Jubilee" to make clear which harvests are counted; verse 16 and the whole law imply it.

records.source: לְפִ֣י׀רֹ֣ב הַשָּׁנִ֗ים תַּרְבֶּה֙ מִקְנָת֔וֹ וּלְפִי֙ מְעֹ֣ט הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תַּמְעִ֖יט מִקְנָת֑וֹ כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר תְּבוּאֹ֔ת ה֥וּא מֹכֵ֖ר לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: According to [the] mouth of the many of the years you will increase its price, and according to [the] mouth of the few of the years you will decrease its price; for [the] number of crops he [is] selling to you.
pieces: If many years are left, the price goes up; if only a few, it goes down. For he is selling you a certain number of harvests.

L.16: According to the abundance of the years you shall increase its price, and according to the fewness of the years you shall decrease its price; for [it is] a number of crops he [is] selling you.

R.16: If there are many years left, the price will be higher. If there are only a few years left, the price will be lower. That is because the seller is only selling you the crops for those years.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of: in proportion to
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of" is a Hebrew idiom for "in proportion to" or "as much as" (Numbers 26:54). The price rises and falls with the years left.

decisions.choice: a number of crops he is selling: the land itself is not sold
decisions.reason: What changes hands is the produce of a number of years, not the land for good. Verse 23 gives the reason: the land belongs to God.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א תוֹנוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־עֲמִית֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And not you will wrong each man his fellow citizen, and you will fear from your God; for I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: So do not cheat one another; fear your God instead. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.17: And you shall not wrong, {{gender:each one|each man}}, his fellow, but you shall fear your God; for I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.17: Do not cheat each other. Respect your God and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: fear your God: revere God and obey him
decisions.reason: To fear God is to hold him in awe and therefore to do what he commands (19:14, 32). It is named here because cheating in a private sale may go unseen by others, but not by God. The same words come again in verses 36 and 43.

decisions.choice: Respect your God and obey him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the meaning of "fear" in two plain words, since a young reader may take "fear" as terror only.

records.source: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֙ אֶת־חֻקֹּתַ֔י וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֥י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֹתָ֑ם וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָבֶֽטַח׃
records.gloss: And you will do my statutes, and my judgments you will keep and you will do them, and you will dwell on the land in security.
pieces: Put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes into practice, and be careful to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. Then you will live in safety on the land.

L.18: And you shall do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments you shall keep and do them, and you shall dwell on the land in security.

R.18: Follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws carefully. Then you will live safely in the land.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments: all of God's laws
decisions.reason: The two words are paired for the whole of God's law, as in 18:4-5 and 19:37. "Statutes" are fixed rules; "judgments" are rulings for the life of the community.

decisions.choice: dwell on the land in security: safety is the fruit of obedience
decisions.reason: Living securely in the land is promised to those who keep the law (26:5). The fear of verse 20, that the sabbath year will bring hunger, is met by this promise.

records.source: וְנָתְנָ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ פִּרְיָ֔הּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם לָשֹׂ֑בַע וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לָבֶ֖טַח עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And will give the land its fruit, and you will eat to fullness and you will dwell in security on it.
pieces: The land will produce its fruit, you will have all you want to eat, and you will be safe living there.

L.19: And the land shall give its fruit, and you shall eat to the full and dwell in security on it.

R.19: The land will give you its crops. You will have plenty to eat, and you will live there safely.

decisions.choice: eat to the full, dwell in security: the blessing of chapter 26
decisions.reason: The same promise is made in 26:5, in the blessings for obedience.

records.source: וְכִ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ מַה־נֹּאכַ֤֖לבַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑ת הֵ֚ן לֹ֣א נִזְרָ֔ע וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱסֹ֖ף אֶת־תְּבוּאָתֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And if you say, what will we eat in the year the seventh? Here! not we will sow and not we will gather our produce.
pieces: You might ask, "What are we to eat in the seventh year, if we are not to sow or bring in our harvest?"

L.20: And if you say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year? Look, we may not sow, nor gather our produce,"

R.20: You might ask, "What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not plant crops or gather a harvest?"

decisions.choice: look: pointing to the problem
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what follows: the law itself forbids sowing and harvesting, so where will food come from? Verses 21-22 give God's answer.

records.source: וְצִוִּ֤יתִי אֶת־בִּרְכָתִי֙ לָכֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֑ית וְעָשָׂת֙ אֶת־הַתְּבוּאָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֖שׁ הַשָּׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will command my blessing for you in the year the sixth, and it will make the produce for the three years.
pieces: I will order {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blessing on you in the sixth year, so that the harvest of that year will be enough to last three years.

L.21: then I will command {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blessing for you in the sixth year, and it shall make the produce for three years.

R.21: I will bless you in the sixth year. The land will give you enough food for three years.

decisions.choice: I will command my blessing: God sends his blessing as a king gives an order
decisions.reason: God's blessing is pictured as a servant sent out at his command (Deuteronomy 28:8; Psalm 133:3). The blessing is the plentiful harvest itself.

decisions.choice: for three years: the sixth, the seventh and the eighth
decisions.reason: The sixth-year harvest feeds the people for the rest of the sixth year, through the seventh when nothing is sown, and through the eighth, when they sow again but must wait for the crop (verse 22). The text does not say how the two fallow years of the Jubilee (verse 11) are provided for.

records.source: וּזְרַעְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמִינִ֔ת וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם מִן־הַתְּבוּאָ֣ה יָשָׁ֑ן עַ֣ד׀הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַתְּשִׁיעִ֗ת עַד־בּוֹא֙ תְּב֣וּאָתָ֔הּ תֹּאכְל֖וּ יָשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: And you will sow the year the eighth and you will eat from the produce old [store] until the year the ninth; until comes its produce you will eat old [store].
pieces: When you sow in the eighth year you will still be eating from the old harvest. You will go on eating the old store until the ninth year, when that year's crop comes in.

L.22: And you shall sow [in] the eighth year and eat from the produce, old [store], until the ninth year; until its produce comes you shall eat old [store].

R.22: In the eighth year you will plant again, but you will still be eating food from the old harvest. You will keep eating it until the new crop comes in, in the ninth year.

decisions.choice: until the ninth year: until the crop sown in the eighth year is harvested
decisions.reason: The crop sown in the autumn of the eighth year is gathered the next spring and summer, counted as the ninth year. Until then the people live on what was stored from the sixth-year harvest.

records.source: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ לֹ֤א תִמָּכֵר֙ לִצְמִתֻ֔ת כִּי־לִ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֧ים וְתוֹשָׁבִ֛ים אַתֶּ֖ם עִמָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And the land not will be sold in perpetuity, for to me [is] the land; for sojourners and settlers you [are] with me.
pieces: No land is to be sold for good, for the land belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are only outsiders and residents living with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.23: And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; for sojourners and settlers you [are] with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.23: Land must never be sold forever, because it belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are only strangers on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, people who live there with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guests.

decisions.choice: the land is mine: God owns the land; Israel holds it from him
decisions.reason: This is the ground of all the laws in the chapter. The land is God's (Exodus 19:5; Psalm 24:1), and he gives it to Israel's families to use (verse 2). No one can sell for good what belongs to God. So land can only be leased until the Jubilee (verses 15-16), and it can always be bought back (verse 24). Naboth's refusal to sell his family's vineyard to the king rests on this law (1 Kings 21:3).

decisions.choice: sojourners and settlers: people who live on land that is not theirs
decisions.reason: A sojourner is a person living in a land not his own (see 16:29; 19:10). A settler is one who has settled among a people without belonging to them, with no land of his own, often working for others (22:10; 25:6, 40). God tells Israel that this is their place before him: they live in his land as his guests and tenants, not its owners. Abraham called himself "a sojourner and settler" among the Hittites (Genesis 23:4), and David uses the same words of his life before God (1 Chronicles 29:15; Psalm 39:13).

decisions.choice: in perpetuity: for good, beyond recall
decisions.reason: The word means finally and completely, so that the seller loses all claim to it. It is used again in verse 30 of a town house that is not bought back in time.

decisions.choice: strangers ... people who live there with me as my guests
decisions.reason: Readable uses the settled "strangers" and "people who live" there, and spells out what "with me" means: Israel lives on God's land as his guests do, not as its owners.

records.source: וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֑ם גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּתְּנ֥וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: And in all [the] land of your possession redemption you will grant for the land.
pieces: Throughout the land you hold, you must allow land that has been sold to be bought back.

L.24: And in all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land.

R.24: Anywhere in your land, if land is sold, the seller's family must have the right to buy it back.

decisions.choice: redemption: the right to buy back
decisions.reason: The word means the right, and the duty, to buy back what has been sold, so that it returns to its first owner. Verses 25-28 say who may do it and how. See verse 25 on the redeemer.

decisions.choice: the seller's family
decisions.reason: Readable names who holds the right: the seller and his relatives (verses 25-27).

records.source: כִּֽי־יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָכַ֖ר מֵאֲחֻזָּת֑וֹ וּבָ֤א גֹֽאֲלוֹ֙ הַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֔יו וְגָאַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מִמְכַּ֥ר אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: If becomes poor your brother and he sells from his possession, and will come his redeemer, the near [one] to him, and he will redeem the thing sold of his brother.
pieces: Suppose a fellow Israelite falls into poverty and has to sell some of his land. Then the relative closest to him, his redeemer, is to come and buy back what his kinsman sold.

L.25: If your brother becomes poor and sells [some] of his possession, then his redeemer, the [one] nearest to him, shall come and redeem what his brother sold.

R.25: Suppose one of your people becomes poor and sells some of his land. Then his closest relative must come and buy it back. That relative is called his redeemer.

decisions.choice: his redeemer: the nearest relative, who must buy back what the family has lost
decisions.reason: The redeemer is the close relative whose duty is to stand up for a member of the family in trouble. He buys back family land that has been sold (here; Jeremiah 32:6-12), buys a relative's freedom (verses 48-49), and, in other passages, takes up the cause of a relative who has been killed (Numbers 35:19). The book of Ruth shows the custom at work: Boaz is a redeemer for Naomi's family, and he buys her land and marries Ruth after the nearer redeemer gives way (Ruth 2:20; 3:9-13; 4:1-10). God calls himself Israel's Redeemer, who frees his family from slavery (Exodus 6:6; Isaiah 41:14).

decisions.choice: your brother: a fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: In these laws "brother" means any fellow Israelite, a member of the one family of God's people. The cases are those of a householder who holds family land ("he and his sons", verses 41 and 54).

decisions.choice: sells some of his possession: part of his land
decisions.reason: The preposition means "some of": he sells only part of his land, as a poor man might do to meet a debt.

decisions.choice: a fellow Israelite / one of your people
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a fellow Israelite, not a brother by birth, so Balanced and Readable say so. In verse 48, where real brothers are meant, all levels say "brothers".

decisions.choice: That relative is called his redeemer
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "redeemer" by explaining it in a short sentence of its own.

records.heading: Buying back land and houses

records.source: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֖וֹ גֹּאֵ֑ל וְהִשִּׂ֣יגָה יָד֔וֹ וּמָצָ֖א כְּדֵ֥י גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And a man, if not there is to him a redeemer, and reaches his hand and he finds as sufficient for its redemption,
pieces: If {{gender:someone|a man}} has no one to redeem it but later prospers and gathers enough to buy it back himself,

L.26: And if {{gender:someone|a man}} has no redeemer, but his hand attains and he finds enough for its redemption,

R.26: Suppose {{gender:someone|a man}} has no relative to buy the land back for him. But later he does well and has enough money to buy it back himself.

decisions.choice: his hand reaches: he becomes able, he can afford it
decisions.reason: The hand stands for a person's means; when the hand "reaches", he can afford something (5:7, 11; 14:21-22). Here the seller himself has recovered enough to buy back his land.

decisions.choice: Suppose ... But later ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long condition into two sentences; the result follows in verse 27.

records.source: וְחִשַּׁב֙ אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י מִמְכָּר֔וֹ וְהֵשִׁיב֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָֽכַר־ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and he will count the years of its sale and he will return the surplus to the man to whom he sold to him, and he will return to his possession.
pieces: he is to work out the years since he sold it, pay the buyer back for the years that remain, and go back to his land.

L.27: then he shall count the years of its sale and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall return to his possession.

R.27: He must count the years since he sold the land. Then he must pay the buyer for the years that are left until the Jubilee. After that, he may go back to his land.

decisions.choice: count the years and return the remainder: pay for the unused years
decisions.reason: The buyer paid for the harvests until the Jubilee (verses 15-16). The seller subtracts the years the buyer has already had and pays back the value of the years still to run.

decisions.choice: until the Jubilee
decisions.reason: Readable says what the remaining years are counted toward, from verses 15-16.

records.source: וְאִ֨ם לֹֽא־מָֽצְאָ֜ה יָד֗וֹ דֵּי֮ הָשִׁ֣יב לוֹ֒ וְהָיָ֣ה מִמְכָּר֗וֹ בְּיַד֙ הַקֹּנֶ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיּוֹבֵ֑ל וְיָצָא֙ בַּיֹּבֵ֔ל וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if not has found his hand sufficient to return to him, and will be his thing sold in [the] hand of the buyer of it until [the] year of the jubilee; and it will go out in the jubilee, and he will return to his possession.
pieces: But if he cannot raise enough to pay him back, the land he sold stays with the buyer until the Jubilee year. In the Jubilee it is released, and he goes back to his land.

L.28: But if his hand has not found enough to repay him, then what he sold shall be in the hand of its buyer until the year of the Jubilee; and it shall go out in the Jubilee, and he shall return to his possession.

R.28: But if he cannot get enough money to pay the buyer back, the land will stay with the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. Then the land will be given back to him, and he can return to it.

decisions.choice: it shall go out: it is released
decisions.reason: "Go out" is the word used of a slave going free (Exodus 21:2-3). The land is pictured in the same way: at the Jubilee it goes free from the buyer and returns to its family. The same word is used of people in verses 41 and 54.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־יִמְכֹּ֤ר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב֙ עִ֣יר חוֹמָ֔ה וְהָיְתָה֙ גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ עַד־תֹּ֖ם שְׁנַ֣ת מִמְכָּר֑וֹ יָמִ֖ים תִּהְיֶ֥ה גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And a man, if he sells a house of dwelling [in] a city of wall, and will be its redemption until is completed [the] year of its sale; days will be its redemption.
pieces: If {{gender:someone|a man}} sells a home inside a walled city, the right to buy it back lasts until a full year has passed since he sold it. He has a year in which to redeem it.

L.29: And if {{gender:someone|a man}} sells a dwelling house [in] a walled city, then its redemption shall be until the completion of a year from its sale; [for a full year of] days shall be its redemption.

R.29: Suppose {{gender:someone|a man}} sells a house inside a city with walls around it. He has one full year after the sale to buy it back.

decisions.choice: a dwelling house in a walled city: a town house, not farmland
decisions.reason: A house in a walled town was not part of a family's farmland, the share of the land that fed it. So it is treated differently: the right to buy it back is short, and it does not return at the Jubilee (verse 30).

decisions.choice: days: a full year
decisions.reason: "Days" is used for a full year, as in 1 Samuel 27:7 and Judges 17:10. The seller has one whole year from the sale.

records.source: וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא־יִגָּאֵ֗ל עַד־מְלֹ֣את לוֹ֮ שָׁנָ֣ה תְמִימָה֒ וְ֠קָם הַבַּ֨יִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִ֜יר אֲשֶׁר־ל֣וֹ חֹמָ֗ה לַצְּמִיתֻ֛ת לַקֹּנֶ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ לְדֹרֹתָ֑יו לֹ֥א יֵצֵ֖א בַּיֹּבֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And if not it is redeemed until is completed for it a year complete, and will stand the house which [is] in the city which [has] to it a wall in perpetuity to the buyer of it for his generations; not it will go out in the jubilee.
pieces: If it is not bought back before the full year is over, the house in the walled city becomes the permanent property of the buyer and his descendants. It is not released in the Jubilee.

L.30: And if it is not redeemed before a full year is completed for it, then the house which [is] in the city that has a wall shall stand in perpetuity for its buyer, for his generations; it shall not go out in the Jubilee.

R.30: If he does not buy it back within that year, the house in the walled city will belong to the buyer forever. It will belong to his children after him too. It will not be given back in the Year of Jubilee.

decisions.choice: which has a wall: following the reading marked for reading aloud
alternatives: which has no wall (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written consonants of the Hebrew text say "which has no wall", but the word is marked to be read "which has a wall". The two words sound alike. The text followed here takes the second reading, which fits the verse: it is the house in a walled city of verse 29 that does not return; houses in open villages do (verse 31).

decisions.choice: shall stand in perpetuity: it becomes the buyer's for good
decisions.reason: "Stand" means to be confirmed or made firm, as of a field that passes to its buyer in Genesis 23:17, 20. "In perpetuity" is the word of verse 23: here, and only here, the sale is final.

records.source: וּבָתֵּ֣י הַחֲצֵרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵין־לָהֶ֤ם חֹמָה֙ סָבִ֔יב עַל־שְׂדֵ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב גְּאֻלָּה֙ תִּהְיֶה־לּ֔וֹ וּבַיֹּבֵ֖ל יֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And the houses of the villages which there is not to them a wall around, on [the] field of the land it will be reckoned; redemption will be for it, and in the jubilee it will go out.
pieces: But a house in a village with no wall around it counts as part of the farmland. The right to buy it back remains, and at the Jubilee it goes back to its owner.

L.31: But the houses of the villages that have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the fields of the land; redemption shall be for it, and in the Jubilee it shall go out.

R.31: But a house in a village without a wall is treated like farmland. It can be bought back at any time, and it must be given back in the Year of Jubilee.

decisions.choice: villages without walls: counted with the open fields
decisions.reason: Unwalled villages were the homes of the farmers who worked the land around them. Their houses belong with the family's land, so the rules for land apply to them (verses 24-28).

decisions.choice: at any time
decisions.reason: Readable states the contrast with verse 29: there is no one-year limit on buying back these houses.

records.source: וְעָרֵי֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בָּתֵּ֖י עָרֵ֣י אֲחֻזָּתָ֑ם גְּאֻלַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And the cities of the Levites, the houses of [the] cities of their possession, a redemption of perpetuity will be for the Levites.
pieces: In the case of the Levites' towns, the houses in the towns they own, the Levites have the right to buy them back at any time.

L.32: And [as for] the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, a perpetual redemption shall be for the Levites.

R.32: The Levites live in their own towns. They may always buy back any house they have sold in those towns.

decisions.choice: the cities of the Levites: the towns given to the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The Levites received no tribal territory but were given towns to live in, with pastureland around them, among the other tribes (Numbers 35:1-8; Joshua 21). Their houses there are their only family property, so the rule for walled cities in verses 29-30 does not apply to them.

decisions.choice: a perpetual redemption: a right to buy back that never runs out
decisions.reason: The word "perpetuity" (as in verse 34) means that the right lasts without limit of time.

records.source: וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִגְאַל֙ מִן־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְיָצָ֧א מִמְכַּר־בַּ֛יִת וְעִ֥יר אֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ בַּיֹּבֵ֑ל כִּ֣י בָתֵּ֞י עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֗ם הִ֚וא אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And what one redeems from the Levites, and will go out [the] sale of a house and a city of his possession in the jubilee; for the houses of [the] cities of the Levites it [is] their possession among [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: And if a house in one of their towns is acquired from a Levite, the sale ends at the Jubilee, for the houses in the Levites' towns are their property among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.33: And what one redeems from the Levites, the sale of a house in a city of his possession, shall go out in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.33: If someone buys a house from a Levite in one of their towns, the house must be given back in the Year of Jubilee. That is because these houses are the only property the Levites have among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: what one redeems from the Levites: what someone acquires from a Levite
alternatives: if one of the Levites redeems it
decisions.reason: The opening is hard. The verb usually means to buy back, but here it seems to mean simply to acquire: whatever house someone takes over from a Levite returns to the Levite at the Jubilee. It may also mean "if one of the Levites redeems", that is, a Levite buys back a house for a relative, and the house still returns to its owner at the Jubilee. The Latin Vulgate reads "if it is not redeemed", which gives a smooth sense but is not the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: a house and a city of his possession: a house in a city he owns
decisions.reason: The phrase joins house and city with "and", but it means the house that stands in a Levite town.

decisions.choice: the only property
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" from verse 32 and Numbers 35:1-8: the Levites had no farmland of their own.

records.source: וּֽשְׂדֵ֛ה מִגְרַ֥שׁ עָרֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יִמָּכֵ֑ר כִּֽי־אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם ה֖וּא לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] field of [the] pasture land of their cities not it will be sold, for a possession of perpetuity it [is] to them.
pieces: The pastureland around their towns may not be sold at all; it is theirs for all time.

L.34: But the field of the pastureland of their cities shall not be sold, for it [is] a perpetual possession for them.

R.34: The fields around their towns where their animals graze must never be sold. They belong to the Levites forever.

decisions.choice: the pastureland: the open land around a Levite town
decisions.reason: The word means the common land around a town, used to graze animals (Numbers 35:2-5 gives its size). It may not be sold even until the Jubilee.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָ֥טָה יָד֖וֹ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהֶֽחֱזַ֣קְתָּ בּ֔וֹ גֵּ֧ר וְתוֹשָׁ֛ב וָחַ֖י עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And if becomes poor your brother and slips his hand with you, and you will strengthen him, a sojourner and settler, and he will live with you.
pieces: If a fellow Israelite near you falls into poverty and can no longer provide for himself, you are to support him, and he is to live beside you like an outsider or a resident.

L.35: And if your brother becomes poor and his hand fails beside you, then you shall support him; [as] a sojourner and settler he shall live with you.

R.35: Suppose one of your people near you becomes poor and cannot take care of himself. Then you must help him. Let him live with you the way strangers and people who live among you do.

decisions.choice: his hand slips: he can no longer support himself
decisions.reason: The hand stands for a person's means (verse 26). When it slips or gives way, he can no longer keep himself.

decisions.choice: strengthen him: take hold of him and support him
decisions.reason: The verb means to make strong or to take a firm hold of. It pictures catching someone who is falling. Verses 36-37 say how: by lending to him without profit.

decisions.choice: a sojourner and settler: the place he is to have while he is poor
alternatives: help him as you would a sojourner and settler
decisions.reason: The words stand without a joining word. They may describe how he is to live with you, as a sojourner and settler does: a free person under your protection, though without land (verse 23). Or they may compare how you help him with how you help the sojourner and settler, who are also to be supported (19:10, 33-34).

records.heading: Caring for the poor

records.source: אַל־תִּקַּ֤ח מֵֽאִתּוֹ֙ נֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּ֔ית וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְחֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Not take from with him interest and increase, and you will fear from your God, and will live your brother with you.
pieces: Do not take interest from him or add anything to what he owes. Fear your God, and let your fellow Israelite keep on living with you.

L.36: Do not take from him interest or increase, but fear your God, and let your brother live beside you.

R.36: Do not charge him interest or make any profit from him. Respect your God, and let your neighbor go on living with you.

decisions.choice: interest and increase: any profit made on a loan to a poor Israelite
decisions.reason: The first word comes from a verb meaning "to bite": interest that eats into what the borrower has. The second means "increase": something added to what is given back. Verse 37 uses the first of money and the second of food. Together they forbid any gain from a loan to a fellow Israelite who is poor (Exodus 22:25; Deuteronomy 23:19-20; Psalm 15:5; Ezekiel 18:8, 13, 17). The aim is not to forbid lending but to make it a help rather than a trap. Deuteronomy 23:20 allows interest from a foreigner, who would borrow for trade rather than from need.

decisions.choice: and your brother shall live: so that he can go on living among you
decisions.reason: The verb form gives the purpose of the command: the loan without interest lets the poor man stay alive and stay in the community.

decisions.choice: your neighbor
decisions.reason: Readable says "your neighbor" for "your brother" here, the fellow Israelite of verse 35.

records.source: אֶ֨ת־כַּסְפְּךָ֔ לֹֽא־תִתֵּ֥ן ל֖וֹ בְּנֶ֑שֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּ֖ית לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן אָכְלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Your silver not you will give to him for interest, and for increase not you will give your food.
pieces: When you lend him money, take no interest, and when you supply him with food, take no extra back.

L.37: Your silver you shall not give him for interest, and for increase you shall not give your food.

R.37: If you lend him money, do not make him pay back more than he borrowed. If you sell him food, do not make a profit on it.

decisions.choice: silver, food: loans of money and of food
decisions.reason: Loans were made in silver, weighed out, and in grain or other food to be repaid from the next harvest. Neither may bring the lender a profit at a poor person's expense.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: "Silver" was the money of the time, so Balanced and Readable say "money".

decisions.choice: sell him food
decisions.reason: "Give food for increase" may mean lending food to be repaid with more, or selling it at a profit. Readable says "sell"; Balanced keeps both open with "supply".

records.source: אֲנִ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: I [am] Yahweh your God, who I brought out you from [the] land of Egypt to give to you [the] land of Canaan, to be for you God.
pieces: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. It was I who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I could give you the land of Canaan and be your God.

L.38: I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.

R.38: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of Egypt. I did it so that I could give you the land of Canaan and be your God.

decisions.choice: who brought you out ... to give you ... to be your God: what God did is the reason for the law
decisions.reason: The poor Israelite is to be helped because God himself rescued all Israel from slavery and gave them the land as a gift. Those who received freely are not to profit from a brother's need. The same reason is given in verses 42 and 55.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָמ֥וּךְ אָחִ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ וְנִמְכַּר־לָ֑ךְ לֹא־תַעֲבֹ֥ד בּ֖וֹ עֲבֹ֥דַת עָֽבֶד׃
records.gloss: And if becomes poor your brother with you and he sells himself to you, not you will make work by him [the] work of a slave.
pieces: Suppose a fellow Israelite living near you becomes so poor that he sells himself to you. You must not make him do a slave's work.

L.39: And if your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him serve the service of a slave.

R.39: Suppose one of your people near you becomes so poor that he sells himself to you to pay what he owes. Do not make him work as a slave.

decisions.choice: sells himself: hires himself out for years to pay a debt
decisions.reason: A man with nothing left to sell could pay his debts by selling his own work, and himself, to a creditor (2 Kings 4:1; Nehemiah 5:1-5). The law limits what this can mean: he works for the buyer, but he is not his property.

decisions.choice: the work of a slave: being owned and worked as property
decisions.reason: The word for slave means a person who belonged to a master, could be bought, sold and passed on to heirs (verses 44-46), and had no right to leave. Such slaves had some protection in law (Exodus 21:20-21, 26-27), but they were owned. An Israelite who sells himself may not be held in that position. He is to be treated as a worker earning wages (verse 40), and he goes free at the Jubilee. The same word is used when God calls Israel "my slaves" in verses 42 and 55: they already belong to him, so they cannot belong to anyone else.

decisions.choice: to pay what he owes
decisions.reason: Readable gives the reason a person sold himself, which the passage implies (verses 25, 35).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: an Israelite who sells himself may not be held as an owned slave (m2).

records.heading: Israelites who sell themselves

records.source: כְּשָׂכִ֥יר כְּתוֹשָׁ֖ב יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֑ךְ עַד־שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל יַעֲבֹ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: As a hired laborer, as a settler he will be with you; until [the] year of the jubilee he will work with you.
pieces: He is to stay with you on the footing of a hired worker or a resident, and work for you up to the Jubilee year.

L.40: As a hired worker, as a settler he shall be with you; until the year of the Jubilee he shall serve with you.

R.40: Treat him like a worker you pay, or like a person who lives among you. He will work for you until the Year of Jubilee.

decisions.choice: as a hired worker, as a settler: free, paid, and with the right to leave
decisions.reason: The hired worker is paid for his work (19:13; Deuteronomy 24:14-15), and the settler is a free person living in another's land (verse 23). The Israelite who has sold himself is to have that standing.

decisions.choice: until the year of the Jubilee: the longest he may serve
decisions.reason: Exodus 21:2 and Deuteronomy 15:12 set the release of a Hebrew slave at the seventh year of service. This law does not mention that limit but sets the Jubilee as the end of all such service, with no slave's status meanwhile. The text does not say how the two laws were applied together.

records.source: וְיָצָא֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֣יו עִמּ֑וֹ וְשָׁב֙ אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־אֲחֻזַּ֥ת אֲבֹתָ֖יו יָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: And he will go out from with you, he and his sons with him, and he will return to his clan, and to [the] possession of his fathers he will return.
pieces: Then he and his {{gender:children|sons}} are to leave you and go back to his clan, and he will return to the land his ancestors held.

L.41: Then he shall go out from you, he and his {{gender:children|sons}} with him, and return to his clan, and to the possession of his fathers he shall return.

R.41: Then he and his {{gender:children|sons}} will be free to leave. He will go back to his clan and to the land that belonged to his family.

decisions.choice: go out, return to his clan and his fathers' possession: freedom and land together
decisions.reason: "Go out" is the word for a slave's release (Exodus 21:2). At the Jubilee the man and his family go free and also get back their family land (verse 28), so that they can live again on their own.

decisions.choice: his sons: his children
decisions.reason: The word can mean sons or children; his whole family goes free with him (Exodus 21:3).

records.source: כִּֽי־עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לֹ֥א יִמָּכְר֖וּ מִמְכֶּ֥רֶת עָֽבֶד׃
records.gloss: For my slaves they [are], whom I brought out them from [the] land of Egypt; not they will be sold [with the] sale of a slave.
pieces: For they are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, since I brought them out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold the way slaves are sold.

L.42: For they [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold [as] a slave is sold.

R.42: The Israelites are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, because I brought them out of Egypt. So no one may sell them as slaves.

decisions.choice: they are my slaves: Israel belongs to God, who bought them out of Egypt
decisions.reason: God freed Israel from slavery in Egypt to make them his own (Exodus 19:4-6; 20:2). They now belong to him as slaves belong to their master, and so no human master can own them. The word is the same as in verse 39 (see there), and it is the word used of Israel in Egypt (Exodus 13:3). Belonging to God is the ground of their freedom from every other owner.

decisions.choice: sold with the sale of a slave: sold outright, as property
decisions.reason: The phrase means a sale that hands a person over as property for good, as at a slave market. An Israelite's service can be sold for a time (verse 39), but not his person.

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant by "they".

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: Israel belongs to God as slaves to their master, and so may not be sold as slaves are sold; the two uses must stay one word (m1, m2).

records.source: לֹא־תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָ֑רֶךְ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Not you will rule over him with harshness, and you will fear from your God.
pieces: Do not lord it over him with cruelty. Fear your God.

L.43: You shall not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your God.

R.43: Do not be a cruel master to him. Respect your God.

decisions.choice: rule with harshness: as Egypt ruled Israel
decisions.reason: The word for harshness is used only of the Egyptians' treatment of Israel (Exodus 1:13-14) and of these laws (verses 46, 53). Israel must not treat a fellow Israelite as Egypt treated them.

decisions.choice: fear your God: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: God sees how a master treats someone in his power, even when no one else does.

records.source: וְעַבְדְּךָ֥ וַאֲמָתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִהְיוּ־לָ֑ךְ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵהֶ֥ם תִּקְנ֖וּ עֶ֥בֶד וְאָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And your slave and your female slave who will be to you from with the nations which [are] around you, from them you will buy slave and female slave.
pieces: If you want male or female slaves, you may buy them from the nations that live around you.

L.44: And your male slave and your female slave whom you may have [shall be] from the nations which [are] around you; from them you may buy male slave and female slave.

R.44: You may buy men and women as slaves from the nations around you.

decisions.choice: male and female slaves from the nations: lifelong slaves, owned as property
decisions.reason: Here the law allows what verses 39-43 forbid for Israelites: slaves bought from other peoples, who did not go free at the Jubilee and could be left to heirs (verse 46). Such a slave belonged to the household. He or she was circumcised and shared the Passover (Exodus 12:44), rested on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:10; Deuteronomy 5:14), was protected from being killed or maimed by the master (Exodus 21:20-21, 26-27), and, if he escaped from a foreign master, was not to be handed back (Deuteronomy 23:15-16). But the slave was owned and could not leave. The text states this plainly, and the decision here is to translate it plainly.

decisions.choice: you may buy: permission, not a command
decisions.reason: The verbs allow the purchase of foreign slaves; they do not require it.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: these slaves are bought and owned for life (m1).

records.source: וְ֠גַם מִבְּנֵ֨י הַתּוֹשָׁבִ֜ים הַגָּרִ֤ים עִמָּכֶם֙ מֵהֶ֣ם תִּקְנ֔וּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמָּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹלִ֖ידוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לַֽאֲחֻזָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And also from [the] sons of the settlers who sojourn with you, from them you will buy, and from their clan which [is] with you which they have fathered in your land; and they will be to you for a possession.
pieces: You may also buy them from the residents who are staying among you, and from their families who are with you and were born in your land. They may be counted among your holdings.

L.45: And also from the sons of the settlers who sojourn with you, from them you may buy, and from their clans that [are] with you, which they have fathered in your land; and they shall be your possession.

R.45: You may also buy slaves from the families of people from other lands who live among you, even those born in your land. They may belong to you.

decisions.choice: the sons of the settlers: settlers and their descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons of" means those who belong to a group, here the families of foreign settlers (see verse 23) living in Israel, including their children born there.

decisions.choice: a possession: property held for good
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of a family's land in verses 10-41. Foreign slaves could be held as permanent property, which is just what an Israelite could not be (verse 42).

decisions.choice: the residents / people from other lands who live among you
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the settled "resident"; Readable says who they are, since "the people who live among you" alone would include Israelites.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable, which names who is bought, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought and owned as property (m2).

records.source: וְהִתְנַחֲלְתֶּ֨םאֹתָ֜ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֤ם אַחֲרֵיכֶם֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֲחֻזָּ֔ה לְעֹלָ֖ם בָּהֶ֣ם תַּעֲבֹ֑דוּ וּבְאַ֨חֵיכֶ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לֹא־תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And you will pass on as an inheritance them to your sons after you to inherit [as] a possession; forever by them you will work; but over your brothers, [the] sons of Israel, each man over his brother, not you will rule over him with harshness.
pieces: You may hand them down to your {{gender:children|sons}} after you as property they will hold, and they may work for you permanently. But over your own kin, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, you must not rule harshly, one over another.

L.46: And you may give them as an inheritance to your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, to inherit [as] a possession; forever you may make them serve; but over your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, {{gender:each one|each man}} over his brother, you shall not rule over him with harshness.

R.46: You may leave these slaves to your {{gender:children|sons}} when you die, and they will belong to them. They can be your slaves for as long as they live. But you must never be cruel masters over your own people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: forever you may make them serve: for life, without release at the Jubilee
decisions.reason: "Forever" here means for as long as the slave lives, and through his descendants; the release of the Jubilee is not for them (see verse 44).

decisions.choice: over your brothers, each over his brother: Israelites are one family
decisions.reason: The contrast closes the section. All Israelites are brothers and sisters in one family under God, and none may become another's master (verses 39-43).

decisions.choice: your own kin
decisions.reason: Balanced says "kin" for "brothers": the word means fellow members of the one people, men and women.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable, as the style guide keeps it where people are owned as property and passed on to heirs (m1).

records.source: וְכִ֣י תַשִּׂ֗יג יַ֣ד גֵּ֤ר וְתוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וּמָ֥ךְ אָחִ֖יךָ עִמּ֑וֹ וְנִמְכַּ֗ר לְגֵ֤ר תּוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ א֥וֹ לְעֵ֖קֶר מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת גֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And if reaches [the] hand of a sojourner and settler with you, and becomes poor your brother with him, and he sells himself to a sojourner settler with you or to an offshoot of [the] clan of a sojourner,
pieces: If an outsider or resident living among you becomes rich, and a fellow Israelite near him grows poor and sells himself to that outsider or to a member of the outsider's clan,

L.47: And if the hand of a sojourner or settler with you attains [wealth], and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the sojourner [or] settler with you or to an offshoot of a sojourner's clan,

R.47: Suppose a stranger who lives among you becomes rich. And suppose one of your people becomes poor and sells himself to that stranger, or to someone in the stranger's family.

decisions.choice: the hand reaches: he becomes wealthy
decisions.reason: As in verse 26, the "hand" that "reaches" means a person who has the means. Here a foreigner living in Israel has prospered.

decisions.choice: an offshoot: a member of a family line
decisions.reason: The word means a root or shoot, and so a descendant or member of a family. The Israelite may have sold himself to the outsider or to one of his relatives.

decisions.choice: a sojourner settler: the same person as before
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and", naming the outsider already mentioned in the verse.

decisions.choice: Suppose ... And suppose ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long condition into two sentences; what follows is in verse 48.

records.heading: Buying back an Israelite sold to an outsider

records.source: אַחֲרֵ֣י נִמְכַּ֔ר גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּהְיֶה־לּ֑וֹ אֶחָ֥ד מֵאֶחָ֖יו יִגְאָלֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: after he has sold himself redemption will be for him; one of his brothers will redeem him,
pieces: he still has the right to be bought back after selling himself. One of his brothers may redeem him,

L.48: after he has sold himself, there shall be redemption for him; one of his brothers may redeem him,

R.48: Even after he has sold himself, he can still be bought back. One of his brothers may buy his freedom.

decisions.choice: there shall be redemption for him: he can be bought back
decisions.reason: An Israelite in the house of a foreign master must not be left there. As family land can be bought back (verse 25), so can a family member. The redeemer of verse 25 has the same duty for persons as for land.

records.source: אוֹ־דֹד֞וֹ א֤וֹ בֶן־דֹּדוֹ֙ יִגְאָלֶ֔נּוּ אֽוֹ־מִשְּׁאֵ֧ר בְּשָׂר֛וֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ יִגְאָלֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־הִשִּׂ֥יגָה יָד֖וֹ וְנִגְאָֽל׃
records.gloss: or his uncle or [the] son of his uncle will redeem him, or any of [the] relatives of his flesh from his clan will redeem him; or reaches his hand, and he will be redeemed.
pieces: an uncle could do it, or a cousin, or any other close relative in his clan. Or if he gets the means, he can buy himself back.

L.49: or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or any relative of his flesh from his clan may redeem him; or [if] his hand attains [enough], he may redeem himself.

R.49: Or his uncle or his cousin may buy him back. Any close relative in his clan may do it. Or if he gets enough money, he may buy his own freedom.

decisions.choice: a relative of his flesh: a blood relative
decisions.reason: "His flesh" means his own family by birth (18:6). The list moves outward from brothers to uncles, cousins and the rest of the clan, the order in which the duty to redeem falls (compare Numbers 27:8-11).

decisions.choice: he will be redeemed: he may redeem himself
decisions.reason: The verb form can be passive or reflexive. After "his hand attains", the sense is that he buys his own freedom, as the seller of land may (verse 26).

records.source: וְחִשַּׁב֙ עִם־קֹנֵ֔הוּ מִשְּׁנַת֙ הִמָּ֣כְרוֹ ל֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְהָיָ֞ה כֶּ֤סֶף מִמְכָּרוֹ֙ בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שָׁנִ֔ים כִּימֵ֥י שָׂכִ֖יר יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he will count with the [one who] bought him from [the] year he sold himself to him until [the] year of the jubilee, and will be [the] silver of his sale by [the] number of years; as [the] days of a hired laborer he will be with him.
pieces: Together with the man who bought him, he is to work out how many years run from the year of the sale to the Jubilee year. The money for his sale is then reckoned by those years, as though his time with the buyer were the time of a hired worker.

L.50: And he shall reckon with the one who bought him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of the Jubilee, and the silver of his sale shall be according to the number of years; as the days of a hired worker it shall be with him.

R.50: He and his master must count the years from when he sold himself until the Year of Jubilee. The price is set by that number of years. His time is valued as if he were a worker paid by the year.

decisions.choice: the silver of his sale by the number of years: the price was wages paid in advance
decisions.reason: The buyer had paid for the man's work until the Jubilee. That price is divided into years, each valued like a hired worker's wage, so that the cost of his freedom can be worked out from the years still to run (verses 51-52).

records.source: אִם־ע֥וֹד רַבּ֖וֹת בַּשָּׁנִ֑ים לְפִיהֶן֙ יָשִׁ֣יב גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ מִכֶּ֖סֶף מִקְנָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: If still many in the years, according to their mouth he will return his redemption from [the] silver of his purchase.
pieces: If there are still many years to go, he is to give back a matching part of the money paid for him to buy his freedom.

L.51: If [there are] still many years, according to them he shall pay back his redemption [price] from the silver of his purchase.

R.51: If there are still many years left, he must pay back a large part of the price paid for him.

decisions.choice: according to their mouth: in proportion to the years
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, "according to the mouth of" means "in proportion to". The more years are left, the larger the share of the price he must pay.

records.source: וְאִם־מְעַ֞ט נִשְׁאַ֧ר בַּשָּׁנִ֛ים עַד־שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל וְחִשַּׁב־ל֑וֹ כְּפִ֣י שָׁנָ֔יו יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־גְּאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if few remain in the years until [the] year of the jubilee, and he will count for him; according to [the] mouth of his years he will return his redemption.
pieces: If only a few years remain before the Jubilee year, he is to reckon them up and pay for his freedom in line with those years.

L.52: And if few remain of the years until the year of the Jubilee, then he shall reckon it with him; according to his years he shall pay back his redemption [price].

R.52: If only a few years are left before the Year of Jubilee, he will count them and pay a smaller amount.

decisions.choice: he shall reckon for him: the price is worked out with the buyer
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the Israelite counts the years with his buyer (as in verse 50) or that the sum is reckoned in his favor. Either way the price falls with the years that remain.

decisions.choice: a smaller amount
decisions.reason: Readable states the result of counting fewer years, from verse 51.

records.source: כִּשְׂכִ֥יר שָׁנָ֛ה בְּשָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יִרְדֶּ֥נּֽוּ בְּפֶ֖רֶךְ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: As a hired laborer of a year in a year he will be with him; not he will rule over him with harshness before your eyes.
pieces: He is to live with the buyer like a worker hired from year to year, and you must not let the buyer treat him harshly while you look on.

L.53: As a worker hired year by year he shall be with him; he shall not rule over him with harshness before your eyes.

R.53: He must be treated like a worker hired for a year at a time. Do not stand by and let the foreigner be a cruel master to him.

decisions.choice: before your eyes: in your sight, without your doing anything
decisions.reason: The foreign master is not under Israel's laws in the same way, so the command is to the Israelites around him: they must not stand by while a brother is treated harshly (see verse 43 on "harshness").

decisions.choice: the buyer / the foreigner
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he shall not rule over him". Balanced and Readable name the master, the outsider of verse 47.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל בְּאֵ֑לֶּה וְיָצָא֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֔ל ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֥יו עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if not he is redeemed by these, and he will go out in [the] year of the jubilee, he and his sons with him.
pieces: Even if no one redeems him by these means, he and his {{gender:children|sons}} are to go free in the Jubilee year.

L.54: And if he is not redeemed by these [means], then he shall go out in the year of the Jubilee, he and his {{gender:children|sons}} with him.

R.54: If he is not bought back in any of these ways, he and his {{gender:children|sons}} will go free in the Year of Jubilee.

decisions.choice: by these: by these means, or by these people
decisions.reason: "These" may be the ways of redemption just listed, or the relatives of verses 48-49 who might redeem him. The sense is the same: if no redemption takes place, the Jubilee frees him anyway.

decisions.choice: he shall go out in the year of the Jubilee: even a foreign master must release him
decisions.reason: The law of release applies to an Israelite whoever his master is: no one in God's land may hold one of God's people for good.

records.source: כִּֽי־לִ֤י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבָדִ֔ים עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אוֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For to me [the] sons of Israel [are] slaves; my slaves they [are], whom I brought out them from [the] land of Egypt; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: For the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are slaves who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, the people I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.55: For to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel [are] slaves; they [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.55: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves, and I brought them out of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: to me the sons of Israel are slaves: the reason for every law of release
decisions.reason: The chapter ends with the ground of all its laws, repeating verse 42 (see there). The land is God's (verse 23), and the people are God's. Neither can be sold for good to anyone else.

decisions.choice: the quotation is closed at the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. God's words that began in verse 2 go on into chapter 26 without a new introduction, and the summary in 26:46 closes the whole address given on Mount Sinai. The quotation marks are closed here at the chapter's end, after the closing formula "I am the LORD your God", so that each chapter can be read on its own.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: as in verse 42, Israel belongs to God as slaves, and so no one else may own them; the word must match the slave laws it grounds (m1).
